sentences.text: Sordes had a wingspan of approximately 0.63 meters, though other measurements estimate it at 60 centimeters.
It possessed a long tail that made up more than half of its body length, ending in an elongated vane.
The skull of this creature was approximately 8 centimeters long.
Unlike many other pterosaurs, Sordes did not possess a head crest.
The fossil of Sordes provided the first unequivocal proof that pterosaurs were covered in hair-like filaments called pycnofibres.
According to Sharov and Unwin, Sordes possessed wing membranes attached to its legs and a membrane connecting the legs.
The holotype specimen of Sordes was discovered in the 1960s at the foothills of the Karatau mountains in Kazakhstan.
The genus Sordes was named in 1971 by the paleontologist Aleksandr Grigorevich Sharov, who intended the name to mean 'hairy devil' rather than the literal Latin translation of 'filth' or 'scum'.

Sordes had specialized dentition with large, pointed front teeth for capturing prey and smaller, numerous rear teeth for crushing, suggesting it ate invertebrates with tough exoskeletons or slippery amphibians.
Researchers suggest that the pycnofibres on Sordes served as insulation, indicating the animal was warm-blooded, and helped create a streamlined flight profile.
Sordes has traditionally been classified within the pterosaur family Rhamphorhynchidae, though the taxonomic classification for Sordes includes the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
Sordes lived during the late Jurassic period (Oxfordian to Kimmeridgian stages) in what is now Kazakhstan, specifically between 161.5 and 154.8 million years ago during the Oxfordian stage.
Some researchers argue that cladistic analyses show Sordes is a more basal pterosaur and does not belong to the family Rhamphorhynchidae.
